record.context_brief: Even convex majorants and snake polynomials
record.original_question: If μ is a continuous even convex nonnegative function on [−1,1], must the snake polynomial associated with μ have a nonnegative expansion in Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1 (Geno Nikolov). If µ ≥ 0 is a continuous even convex function in [−1, 1], then the associated with µ snake polynomials have non-negative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu:[-1,1]\to[0,\infty)$ be a continuous, even, convex function. The snake polynomial of degree $n$ associated with $\mu$ is the (unique) algebraic polynomial $S_n$ of degree $n$ with leading coefficient $2^{n-1}$ that is bounded in absolute value by $\mu$ on $[-1,1]$ and achieves the equioscillation property $S_n(x_k)=(-1)^{n-k}\mu(x_k)$ at $n+1$ points $-1\le x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_n\le 1$ (so that $S_n$ "snakes" between $-\mu$ and $\mu$). Write the Chebyshev expansion
$$S_n(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} c_k\, T_k(x),$$
where $T_k$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind of degree $k$.

Prove or disprove: for every such $\mu$ and every $n\ge 0$, all coefficients $c_k$ are nonnegative.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this conjecture (attributed to Geno Nikolov) was located via web search; only related work by Nikolov on Chebyshev polynomial inequalities appears, with no result confirming or refuting the nonnegativity of Chebyshev coefficients of snake polynomials for continuous even convex majorants. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some inequalities for Chebyshev polynomials (G. Nikolov)
status_evidence.snippet: Nikolov's related work concerns inequalities for Chebyshev polynomials but does not address the snake polynomial Chebyshev-coefficient nonnegativity conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the snake-polynomial Chebyshev nonnegativity conjecture found in Nikolov's related publications.
